category_title: Students with externalizing behavior problems including work refusal and temper tantrums
scenario_title: Managing increasing difficulty of academic work
minimal_context: The student is seated at a cluster of desks in the TLC classroom and is asked to complete an academic worksheet that increases in difficulty.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please take a pencil from the communal stationery and start on the next section of the worksheet. The questions get a bit harder here.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Pushes the worksheet away) I'm not doing it.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Why don't you just give it a try?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: No. I'm not participating in this.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You need to finish this assignment before the end of class.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Knocks the communal stationery off the desk cluster) I'm not doing this work! It's too hard and I don't care!

dialogue_combined:

task.content: Managing the increasing difficulty of their academic work
task.learning_goal: Succeeding in school and improving academic achievement and social competence

context.social_setting: Seated in such a way as to facilitate small group work, in clusters of desks

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: Where students fail to regulate their behaviour or manage the increasing difficulty of their academic work
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Exhibiting behaviours that made full-participation in the classroom difficult, such as truancy or work refusal
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Sense of efficacy about succeeding in school can decrease, becoming entrenched in a downward cycle

behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Increased classroom disruption, absenteeism/truancy and exclusions, as well as low academic standards and non-participation
